title: rtpproxy Module
content_markdown: This module is used by OpenSIPS to communicate with RTPProxy, a media relay proxy used to make the communication between user agents behind NAT possible. This module is also used along with RTPProxy to record media streams between user agents or to play media to either UAc or UAs.
overview: This module is used by OpenSIPS to communicate with RTPProxy, a media relay proxy used to make the communication between user agents behind NAT possible. This module is also used along with RTPProxy to record media streams between user agents or to play media to either UAc or UAs.
how_it_works: Currently, the rtpproxy module can support multiple rtpproxies for balancing/distribution and control/selection purposes. The module allows the definition of several sets of rtpproxies - load-balancing will be performed over a set and the user has the ability to choose what set should be used. The balancing inside a set is done automatically by the module based on the weight of each rtpproxy from the set. The module can also receive timeout notifications from multiple rtpproxies. RTPProxy can be configured to send notifications when a session doesn't receive any media for a configurable interval of time. The rtpproxy modules has implemented a listener for such notifications and when received it terminates the dialog at SIP level (send BYE to both ends), with the help of dialog module.

dependencies_required.name: a database module
dependencies_required.reason: only if you want to load use a database table from where to load the rtp proxies sets.

dependencies_required.name: dialog module
dependencies_required.reason: if using the rtpproxy_engage functions or RTPProxy timeout notifications.

exported_parameters.name: rtpproxy_sock
exported_parameters.description:
Definition of socket(s) used to connect to (a set) RTPProxy. It may specify a UNIX socket, an IPv4/IPv6 UDP socket or an IPv4/IPv6 TCP socket. If the protocol part (i.e. “udp:”) is missing, the socket is treated as a UNIX socket.

The definition also supports to specify a different IP that will be advertised instead of the one returned by RTPProxy. This is useful when having multiple RTPProxy servers that are located behind NAT, and listen only on private intefaces, but need to advertise a public one.
exported_parameters.example_code:
# single rtpproxy with specific weight
modparam("rtpproxy", "rtpproxy\_sock", "udp:localhost:22222=2")

# single rtpproxy with advertised address + weight
modparam("rtpproxy", "rtpproxy\_sock", "udp:localhost:22222|8.8.8.8=2")

# multiple rtproxies for LB
modparam("rtpproxy", "rtpproxy\_sock",
	"udp:localhost:22222 udp:localhost:22223 tcp:remote1:33422 tcp6:remote2:32322")

# multiple sets of multiple rtproxies
modparam("rtpproxy", "rtpproxy\_sock", "1 == udp:localhost:22222 udp:localhost:22223")
modparam("rtpproxy", "rtpproxy\_sock", "2 == udp:localhost:22223")
modparam("rtpproxy", "rtpproxy\_sock", "2 == udp:localhost:22223|8.8.8.8")

exported_parameters.name: rtpproxy_disable_tout
exported_parameters.description: Once RTPProxy was found unreachable and marked as disable, rtpproxy will not attempt to establish communication to RTPProxy for rtpproxy\_disable\_tout seconds.

exported_parameters.name: rtpproxy_timeout
exported_parameters.description: Timeout value in waiting for reply from RTPProxy.

exported_parameters.name: rtpproxy_autobridge
exported_parameters.description: Enable auto-bridging feature. Does not properly function when doing serial/parallel forking!

exported_parameters.name: rtpproxy_retr
exported_parameters.description: How many times rtpproxy should retry to send and receive after timeout was generated.

exported_parameters.name: default_set
exported_parameters.description: The parameter indicates the default RTPProxy set to be used when provisioning an engine in the config file without an explicit set, or when calling one of the _rtpproxy\_*()_ functions without an explicit set.

exported_parameters.name: nortpproxy_str
exported_parameters.description:
The parameter sets the SDP attribute used by rtpproxy to mark the packet SDP informations have already been mangled.

If empty string, no marker will be added or checked.
exported_parameters.notes: The string must be a complete SDP line, including the EOH (\r\n).

exported_parameters.name: db_url
exported_parameters.description: The database url. This parameter should be set if you want to use a database table from where to load or reload definitions of socket(s) used to connect to (a set) RTPProxy. The record from the database table will be read at start up (added to the ones defined with the rtpproxy\_sock module parameter) and when the MI command rtpproxy\_reload is issued(the definitions will be replaced with the ones from the database table).

exported_parameters.name: db_table
exported_parameters.description: The name of the database table containing definitions of socket(s) used to connect to (a set) RTPProxy.

exported_parameters.name: rtpp_socket_col
exported_parameters.description: The name rtpp socket column in the database table.

exported_parameters.name: set_id_col
exported_parameters.description: The name set id column in the database table.

exported_parameters.name: rtpp_notify_socket
exported_parameters.description: The socket OpenSIPS listens for notifications from RTPProxy. Currently OpenSIPS can receive RTP timeout and DTMF events.
exported_parameters.example_code:
modparam("rtpproxy", "rtpp_notify_socket", "tcp:10.10.10.10:9999")

# use an UNIX socket
modparam("rtpproxy", "rtpp_notify_socket", "unix:/tmp/rtpproxy.unix")
# or
modparam("rtpproxy", "rtpp_notify_socket", "/tmp/rtpproxy.unix")

exported_parameters.name: generated_sdp_port_min
exported_parameters.description: When RTPProxy module needs to generate an SDP body, use this value as the minimum value of the port.

exported_parameters.name: generated_sdp_port_max
exported_parameters.description: When RTPProxy module needs to generate an SDP body, use this value as the maximum value of the port.

exported_parameters.name: generated_sdp_media_ip
exported_parameters.description: When RTPProxy module needs to generate an SDP body, use this value as the media_ip in the c= and the o=.

exported_functions.name: rtpproxy_engage

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: flags to turn on some features.

parameters.name: ip_address
parameters.description: new SDP IP address.

parameters.name: set_id
parameters.description: the set used for this call.

parameters.name: sock_var
parameters.description: variable used to store the RTPProxy socket chosen for this call. Note that the variable will only be populated in the initial request.

parameters.name: ret_var
parameters.description: variable used to print the IP and port the RTPProxy server is using for this call. This is useful especially when using the _rtp_cluster_, which can advertise multiple servers behind it. The format of the value returned is _IP:port_. Note that the variable will only be populated in the initial request.

exported_functions.description: Rewrites SDP body to ensure that media is passed through an RTP proxy. It uses the dialog module facilities to keep track when the rtpproxy session must be updated. Function must only be called for the initial INVITE and internally takes care of rewriting the body of 200 OKs and ACKs. Note that when used in bridge mode, this function might advertise wrong interfaces in SDP (due to the fact that OpenSIPS is not aware of the RTPProxy configuration), so you might face an undefined behavior.

exported_functions.name: rtpproxy_stream2uac

parameters.name: prompt_name
parameters.description: name of the prompt to stream. Should be either absolute pathname or pathname relative to the directory where RTPproxy runs.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: number of times the prompt should be repeated. The value of -1 means that it will be streaming in loop indefinitely, until appropriate `rtpproxy_stop_stream2xxx` is issued.

parameters.name: set_id
parameters.description: the set used for this call.

parameters.name: sock_var
parameters.description: variable used to store the RTPProxy socket chosen for this call.

exported_functions.description: Instruct the RTPproxy to stream prompt/announcement pre-encoded with the makeann command from the RTPproxy distribution. The uac/uas suffix selects who will hear the announcement relatively to the current transaction - UAC or UAS. For example invoking the `rtpproxy_stream2uac` in the request processing block on ACK transaction will play the prompt to the UA that has generated original INVITE and ACK while `rtpproxy_stop_stream2uas` on 183 in reply processing block will play the prompt to the UA that has generated 183. Apart from generating announcements, another possible application of this function is implementing music on hold (MOH) functionality. When count is -1, the streaming will be in loop indefinitely until the appropriate `rtpproxy_stop_stream2xxx` is issued. In order to work correctly, functions require that the session in the RTPproxy already exists. Also those functions don't alted SDP, so that they are not substitute for calling `rtpproxy_offer` or `rtpproxy_answer`.

exported_functions.description:
Instruct the RTPproxy to stream prompt/announcement pre-encoded with the makeann command from the RTPproxy distribution. The uac/uas suffix selects who will hear the announcement relatively to the current transaction - UAC or UAS. For example invoking the `rtpproxy_stream2uac` in the request processing block on ACK transaction will play the prompt to the UA that has generated original INVITE and ACK while `rtpproxy_stop_stream2uas` on 183 in reply processing block will play the prompt to the UA that has generated 183.

Apart from generating announcements, another possible application of this function is implementing music on hold (MOH) functionality. When count is -1, the streaming will be in loop indefinitely until the appropriate `rtpproxy_stop_stream2xxx` is issued.

In order to work correctly, functions require that the session in the RTPproxy already exists. Also those functions don't alted SDP, so that they are not substitute for calling `rtpproxy_offer` or `rtpproxy_answer`.

exported_functions.name: rtpproxy_start_recording

parameters.name: set_id
parameters.description: the set used for this call.

parameters.name: sock_var
parameters.description: variable used to store the RTPProxy socket chosen for this call.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: a list of flags passed to RTPProxy for the recording. Currently only _s_ is supported, and it indicates that RTPProxy should record both audio legs in a single file. Note that this feature is available starting with RTPProxy 2.0.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: the destination of the recording. If it has the _udp:IP:port_ format, RTPProxy sends the RTP stream to that _IP:port_ remote destination. Otherwise, destination represents the name of the file in the recording directory.

parameters.name: mediastream
parameters.description: this parameter is only used if the _destination_ is specified, and represents the index of media stream to record/copy, starting from 1. If this parameter is missing, OpenSIPS instructs RTPProxy to copy all the streams.

exported_functions.description: This command will send a signal to the RTP-Proxy to record the RTP stream on the RTP-Proxy.

exported_functions.description: This command gathers call RTP statistics from RTP-Proxy.

examples.code:
rtpproxy_stats($var(up),$var(down),$var(sent),$var(fail));
xlog("RTP statistics for $ci: up=$var(up) down=$var(down) sent=$var(sent) fail=$var(fail)\n");

parameters.name: set_id

exported_functions.description:
This command gathers all RTP statistics available from RTP-Proxy. All the returned values stored in an AVP that can be further read by indexing the AVP.

This command is only available starting with RTPProxy 2.1 realease.

exported_mi_functions.name: rtpproxy_enable

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: the rtp proxy url (exactly as defined in the config file).

parameters.name: enable
parameters.description: 1 - enable, 0 - disable. the config file).

parameters.name: setid
parameters.description: the rtpproxy set ID (used for better indentification of the rtpproxy instance to be enabled, for example when a rtpproxy is used in multiple sets).

exported_mi_functions.description:
Enables/Disables a rtp proxy.

NOTE: if a rtpproxy is defined multiple times (in the same or different set), all its instances will be enables/disabled IF no set ID provided (as second param).

examples.description: disable a RTPProxy by URL only
disable a RTPProxy by URL and set ID (3)

exported_mi_functions.name: rtpproxy_show
exported_mi_functions.description: Displays all the rtp proxies and their information: set and status (disabled or not, weight and recheck\_ticks).

exported_mi_functions.name: rtpproxy_reload
exported_mi_functions.description: Reload rtp proxies sets from database. The function will delete all previous records and populate the list with the entries from the database table. The db\_url parameter must be set if you want to use this command.

exported_events.name: E_RTPPROXY_STATUS
exported_events.description: This event is raised when a RTPProxy server changes it's status to enabled/disabled.

parameters.name: socket
parameters.description: the socket that identifies the RTPProxy instance.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: active if the RTPProxy instance responds to probing or inactive if the instance was deactivated.

exported_events.name: E_RTPPROXY_DTMF
exported_events.description: This event is raised when a RTPProxy server sends a DTMF notification to OpenSIPS. In order to catch RFC 2833/4733 DTMF events, you need to provide the d flag to rtpproxy_offer()/ rtpproxy_answer().

parameters.name: digit
parameters.description: the digit pressed.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: the duration of the event.

parameters.name: volume
parameters.description: the volume of the event.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: represents the identifier of the call for which that event was received.

parameters.name: is_callid
parameters.description: is 0 if the id parameter represents the Dialog ID, or 1 if it is a callid.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: indicates the stream index of the RTPProxy session. It is normally 0 if the caller sent the DTMF, or 1 if the callee sent it.

# single rtpproxy with specific weight

	"udp:localhost:22222 udp:localhost:22223 tcp:remote1:33422 tcp6:remote2:32322")
